title: A fork of this repository shows codesweep-ai's name, and previews codesweep-ai's runs
foundBy: user report (session): "On the dashboard, make sure that it can work in a fork as well, and give an accurate dashboard view of the status of the fork, without hardcoding references to the codesweep-ai org."

evidence.verified:
`make ci` passed at a33e346, with 95 unit tests where there were 89. Reverting each of five fixes in a scratch copy failed the new test written for it.

The collector ran over one account's forks of ledger, lint and ui, with `--owner` naming that account. It read each fork at its own head. It found the same internal dependencies as a run over codesweep-ai: 3, 2 and 11. Its compare links and its decline target named that account. The dependencies page rendered that file in headless Chromium, with every repository link on that account and the codesweep-ai title.

The live build at a33e346 read its previous file from https://codesweep.ai/dashboards/deps.json and carries three days of history. The Makefile derives OWNER=alice when GITHUB_REPOSITORY is alice/dashboards. No fork has Pages enabled, so a deployed fork was not tried.

resolution: The collector takes `--owner` and `--site` apart from `org`, so a fork's build reads its own owner's repositories and its own history. The codesweep-ai modules, packages and images still count as siblings. `make status` and `make test` read the checkout's own owner. Every page keeps the codesweep-ai name.
details:
The CI page itself already reads a fork's own data. Every path in `projects.json` is relative, so a fork served at `<owner>.github.io/dashboards/` fetches `<owner>.github.io/<project>/ci-status.json`, which that owner's fork of the project publishes.

Three things still name codesweep-ai. `projects.json` sets the title to `codesweep-ai CI`, and `ci.html` carries the same name, so a fork's tab says it is codesweep-ai's. `make status` and `make test` read `codesweep-ai/<project>` from the API, so a fork's preview shows the upstream runs rather than its own. SPEC.md places every status file under `codesweep.ai`, which is true of one deployment only.

notes.text: The codesweep-ai name is not part of the defect. The repository owner wants every page to keep it in a fork, so the title in `projects.json` and `ci.html` stays. Only where a page reads its data from has to follow the fork.

The dependencies page had the deeper form of this. The collector's `org` both named whose repositories to clone and which modules and packages count as siblings. A fork keeps codesweep-ai's module paths and npm scope, so it could not change `org` without losing its siblings. Its build also read upstream's previous `deps.json`, so a fork's history never accumulated.
